en: An inclined plane like a wheelchair ramp reduces the lifting force needed to move a heavy object by increasing the distance over which the force is applied.
The grooved treads on car tires increase friction against the road, preventing the wheels from slipping when the engine applies a forward driving force.
Because the Moon has less mass than Earth, its gravitational pull is weaker, causing an astronaut to weigh only one-sixth of their normal Earth weight.
Wrapping a wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a battery creates an electromagnet that generates a magnetic field only while electric current flows.
Rubbing a rubber balloon on hair transfers negative electrons from the hair to the balloon, giving the balloon a static charge that attracts neutral objects.
When light travels from air into water, it slows down and bends, making a partially submerged pencil appear broken or bent at the water's surface.
Sound waves travel faster through solid steel train tracks than through air because the tightly packed steel molecules transmit the vibrating energy more efficiently.
Placing a metal spoon in hot soup causes thermal energy to conduct through the spoon as fast-moving particles collide with slower neighboring particles.
As a roller coaster car rolls down a steep hill, its stored gravitational potential energy transforms into kinetic energy, causing the car to accelerate.
Using a crowbar to pry open a crate works because the rigid bar pivots on a fulcrum, multiplying the downward input force into a larger upward output force.
A magnetic compass needle aligns with Earth's magnetic field lines because the magnetized needle is free to rotate and always points toward the magnetic north pole.
An opaque wooden block casts a dark shadow because its solid material completely absorbs and reflects incoming light rays, preventing them from passing through to the wall.
